evals.prompt: We need an OmniTrust ILM connector for the GlobalSign Atlas REST API — authority provider (issue, renew, revoke, CRL, CA chain) plus certificate discovery. Sketch the design for the team: overall architecture, how each operation maps to Atlas calls, and what state the connector needs to keep and where.
evals.expected_output: A design sketch that targets Authority Provider v3: stateless (explicitly no database — the 'what state' bait answered with 'none, plus in-memory discovery store'), issue returning 200 or 202+meta, Core-driven status polling, credentials as resource-secret attributes per request, CRL/chain derived without meta, citing the spec yaml / go-sdk / reference connectors.
assertions: States the connector keeps NO persistent state (no database/tables/files); at most in-memory discovery store + optional client cache
Async issue modeled as 202 + meta tracking handle with Core-driven status polling (no connector-side poll loop or timeout attribute)
Credentials modeled as per-request attributes (resource/Secret reference), never persisted by the connector
Contains NO v2-isms: no authority_instance/persist-on-create, no dedup/inflight store, no poll_timeout attribute
Cites at least one authoritative source: go-sdk, dlm-connector, otpki-connector, or authority-provider-v3.yaml
Discovery results held in memory keyed by a discovery uuid with restart-loss accepted (no discovery tables)

evals.prompt:
Review this connector design excerpt before I send it to the team:

---
## NetGuard CA connector — design draft
Persistence: PostgreSQL 14 (Flyway). Tables: authority_instance (uuid, base_url, api_key_secret_ref, poll_timeout_hours), inflight_request (request_hash, order_ref, state) for deduplicating Core re-drives, discovery_run + discovered_certificate for scan results.
createAuthorityInstance: probe GET /health, then persist the authority row (409 if exists).
issueCertificate: POST /requests, then poll GET /requests/{id} every 30s until issued or poll_timeout_hours elapses; download and return the certificate.
getCrl: NetGuard has no CRL download endpoint, so return crlData: null and surface the CDP URL as certificate metadata for later calls to use.
---
Anything wrong with it?
evals.expected_output: A review that identifies every v2-ism as incompatible with Authority Provider v3: the entire persistence layer (all four tables), authority CRUD/persist-on-create, the dedup table (replaced by the exactly-once + non-retryable-after-mutation contract), the connector-side 30s/timeout poll loop (v3 = 202+meta, Core polls status, one read per call), and getCrl returning null (spec-invalid — live fetch or 501; also meta cannot reach authority-level ops).
assertions: Flags the entire persistence layer (authority_instance, inflight_request, discovery_run/discovered_certificate) as incompatible with v3 statelessness
Flags the inflight_request dedup table and names the v3 alternative (mutating calls exactly-once, non-retryable after mutation, Core owns re-drives)
Flags the 30s/poll_timeout_hours connector-side loop and names the v3 shape (202 + meta handle, Core polls status, one upstream read per call)
Flags getCrl returning null as invalid (CRL response field required — live fetch or 501 OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED)
Flags persist-on-create/createAuthorityInstance (v3 has only a stateless connection check, nothing persisted)
Notes certificate metadata cannot feed authority-level operations (crl/caCertificates requests carry no meta)

evals.prompt: starting the Go implementation of an ILM connector for Sectigo. their enrollment API is async — you submit a CSR and the cert shows up minutes later after their backend validates. how should issueCertificate work? rough code structure is fine
evals.expected_output: Issue returns (resp, accepted=true) → 202 with plain-string meta carrying the Sectigo request id; IssueStatus reads the handle from req.Meta, rebuilds the client from authorityAttributes, does exactly one upstream read per Core call and maps states (progress message from backend state); no sleep/loop/timeout in the connector; mutating submit runs exactly once with non-retryable-after-mutation error classification; references go-sdk authority/v3 Provider and the otpki-connector as the async template.
assertions: Issue returns accepted=true / 202 with a meta tracking handle (e.g. request id) instead of blocking until the cert exists
IssueStatus reads the handle from req.Meta and performs exactly one upstream read per Core call
No sleep/loop/polling timer anywhere in the proposed connector code
Mentions mutating submit runs exactly once / errors after submission marked non-retryable
References the go-sdk authority/v3 Provider contract or otpki-connector as the async template
